answer.rationale: Rated against the primary objective — sustainable long-term qualified revenue — not against whatever local metric each memory reports. memory_57 is strongest: it names revenue explicitly, qualifies it as 'qualified,' and is the only entry that checks a durability counterfactual (no measurable harm to retention), though 'established customers' limits transferability to the SMB churn now under competitive attack. memory_44 is next: pipeline quality is a genuine proxy for qualified revenue and it is comparative (demo-request vs self-serve), but it stops at pipeline and never follows through to closed or retained revenue. memory_86 links onboarding to completion and time-to-value and at least gestures at adoption, but adoption is upstream of revenue and no retention or monetization figure is given. memory_73 reports 'strong acquisition and revenue lift' yet omits margin, discount duration, and what happens when promotional pricing lapses — discount-driven acquisition in a price-sensitive segment is precisely the case where short-run revenue and sustainable revenue can diverge, so the headline revenue claim is weaker evidence than it appears. memory_91 measures week-one engagement and 'first meaningful action,' both early proxies with no stated path to revenue. memory_31 is weakest: it measures first-week activation only, and although it calls the lift 'durable,' durability is asserted over a first-week window with no revenue, conversion, or retention outcome attached — the narrowest metric with the largest unsupported leap to the objective. Two structural caveats apply across the whole set. First, every memory is 'source archived,' so none of the underlying effect sizes, sample sizes, or confidence intervals can be re-examined; these ratings score the strength of the written claim, not verified fact. Second, the memories are uniformly positive — six wins, no recorded failures or null results — which is a signature of survivorship in the consolidation process, so the set likely overstates how reliably these levers work. Relevance to today's situation is a separate axis from evidentiary support and should not be conflated: memory_73 speaks most directly to the competitor's pricing move but is among the weakest evidence for sustainable revenue, which is exactly the tension to hold when choosing the single experiment.
